note: Every place gofbp deliberately does not give cffdrs' answer, and which side is right. Read by internal/oracle; see testdata/README.md. Order is precedence: a row two entries match belongs to the first.

divergences.cffdrs: fbp()'s TROS is ROS(1-E)/(1-E cos(THETA - RAZ)) with THETA converted to radians and RAZ still in degrees, so the cosine is of a meaningless angle. TROSt, TCFB, TFI, TTFC and TTI are all built on it.
divergences.gofbp: Does not produce TROS or anything built on it. ROSAtAngle is the rate at a bearing, taking the bearing relative to the head direction (THETA - RAZ here).
divergences.correct: GLC-X-10 eq. 94 at the relative bearing THETA - RAZ, about the ignition point. Even with the units fixed, TROS is the focus-polar form of the ellipse, which is not eq. 94.
divergences.authority: Wotton, Alexander & Taylor (2009), GLC-X-10, eq. 94 and Table 3, p. 20

divergences.cffdrs: rate_of_spread_at_theta() wraps both leading terms of eq. 94 in one parenthesis before multiplying by the bracket, which collapses them to ROS/cos(THETA): a pole at 90 and 270 degrees and negative rates behind the flanks.
divergences.gofbp: ROSAtAngle solves the ray from the ignition point against the ellipse, which equals the published eq. 94 everywhere it is defined and is finite at 90 degrees.
divergences.correct: Eq. 94 as printed: only the second leading term multiplies the bracket. That grouping reproduces the paper's own Table 3; cffdrs' does not.
divergences.authority: Wotton, Alexander & Taylor (2009), GLC-X-10, eq. 94 and Table 3, p. 20

divergences.cffdrs: Back-solves the slope-equivalent wind from rate_of_spread(), which for C6 is the crown-blended rate, then inverts C6's surface curve with it. Its sloped C6 ISI, WSV and everything downstream move with FMC and CBH.
divergences.gofbp: Predict returns ErrC6OnSlope. NetEffectiveWind is surface-only for every fuel, so it cannot give cffdrs' sloped C6 numbers.
divergences.correct: Unknown. No independent source has been checked for C6's slope-equivalent wind, so neither answer is verified; gofbp refuses rather than give a second unverified one.

divergences.cffdrs: As c6-on-slope: fbpRaster() is fbp() per cell.
divergences.gofbp: PredictGrid refuses the cell with ErrC6OnSlope.

divergences.cffdrs: A code outside 1-19, or NA, becomes C2 with a warning, and the cell is computed as C2.
divergences.gofbp: PredictGrid refuses the cell with ErrGridFuelCode.
divergences.correct: No answer: the cell does not say what fuel it is, and C2 is a guess.
divergences.gap: Fuel codes outside 1-19 in a grid

divergences.cffdrs: NF and WA come back as all zeros with FD NA.
divergences.gofbp: Refused with ErrUnknownFuel, by PredictGrid and Predict alike.
divergences.correct: No answer: NF and WA are not fuels, and a zero rate is indistinguishable from a computed calm-weather zero.

divergences.cffdrs: An NA in any other layer gets fbp()'s default for that input, silently.
divergences.gofbp: PredictGrid refuses a cell whose NA it cannot stand for, and otherwise computes it; a computed cell must then match cffdrs.
divergences.correct: No answer where the default is a guess about the site. Where the input is unused by the cell, both answers are the same.

divergences.cffdrs: A cell NA in every layer is dropped by as.data.table(), and fbpRaster() assigns the shorter result back by position, so every later cell takes the next cell's answer and the last takes cell 1's.
divergences.gofbp: Refuses that cell with ErrGridFuelCode and leaves every other cell as it would be without it.
divergences.correct: One answer per cell, at that cell: fbpRaster()'s own contract.
divergences.held_by_generator: gen_cffdrs_reference.R stops if fbpRaster() no longer shifts the cells, so a cffdrs that fixes this fails the regeneration rather than this register

divergences.cffdrs: fbp() returns NA for D2's rates.
divergences.gofbp: Refused as an unknown fuel with ErrUnknownFuel, not reported as zero.
divergences.correct: No answer: neither cffdrs nor this package has coefficients for D2, so there is nothing to compute a rate from.

divergences.cffdrs: fbp() takes an ISI that overrides the computed one, and a BUIEFF switch that turns the buildup effect off.
divergences.gofbp: No such inputs: Predict always computes ISI from FFMC and the net effective wind, and always applies the buildup effect.
divergences.correct: Not a disagreement about a number: with the overrides at their defaults the two agree, and every fixture row sends the defaults.

divergences.cffdrs: 1.9.2 rounds a caller-supplied D0 half-to-even (150.7 becomes 151); upstream HEAD rounds only a computed one.
divergences.correct: The pinned oracle, until the provenance question in MIGRATION.md's open drift note is decided. Integer dates are unaffected either way.
